newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala court convicts former vice president.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala court convicts former vice president.

text.p: Former vice president Gustavo Espina was sentenced to four years in prison or a $1,200 fine on Tuesday for violating the constitution during a 1993 "coup" engineered by then-president Jorge Serrano in 1993.
The trial marked the first time in the nation's history that a vice president was tried for actions committed during his term.

"Guilty of the crime of violating the constitution," the court secretary read in open court. "For the crime...the court imposes a four-year prison sentence, commutable to five quetzales ($.83) a day."
Espina is also barred from public office during the years of his sentence.

During six days of trial testimony this month the three judges of the Fourth Criminal Sentence Court heard from former cabinet ministers who said Espina appeared to play no part in Serrano's attempt to seize dictatorial powers in May 1993.
But state prosecutors said Espina supported Serrano's actions by appearing at a news conference when the president announced he was dissolving Congress and the Supreme Court.
Espina, who did not testify, said that although he remained in Serrano's administration during the crisis and appeared in public with the president, he did not help plan or execute Serrano's scheme.
On May 25, 1993, Serrano called his ministers to an emergency meeting and informed them he was dissolving the legislature in an effort to take control of spiraling government corruption.

The "self-coup" was a blow to Guatemala's struggle for democracy. A series of generals had ruled Guatemala for three decades and Serrano was only the second elected civilian president since the 1950s.
Within days of the announcement the military removed Serrano. Congress elected Ramiro de Leon Carpio president.
Espina spent almost two years in exile in Costa Rica before returning to Guatemala to face charges.
Serrano lives in exile in Panama. Guatemala is trying for the third time to extradite him to face charges related to the coup.
